newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Belize-flagged ship sinks off S. African coast.
newsitem.headline: Belize-flagged ship sinks off S. African coast.

text.p: A Belize-registered ship sank in the south Atlantic about 680 miles off the South African coast early on Friday and all 28 crewmen were reported to have abandoned the vessel, rescue officials said.
South African Air Force spokeswoman Marietta Hopley said a C-130 Hercules had left for the scene carrying liferafts and supplies to support the crew until the first ship reached the area on Saturday.
The vessel was believed to be a bulk carrier. The nationalities of the crew were not known.
Hopley said the ship went down 680 miles west of Cape Town about five hours after transmitting a call for help at 23:45 GMT on Thursday. Weather conditions were said to be reasonable.

"The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in Australia passed us the Mayday message. All it said was that the ship was flooding and that the crew were abandoning ship. There were no injuries," she said.
It was not known whether the crew were in the water or in liferafts.
Alan Moore, superintendent of the Cape Town Radio maritime radio service, said three ships -- the Captain Panagiotis, the Southgate and the Cape Falcon -- were heading for the scene.
